title: Death Cults & Psychopomps

slides.text: Who comes for you when you die?
The jackal-headed god weighs your heart against the feather of Ma'at. Too heavy, and Ammit devours it.
Hermes Psychopompos, guide of souls, leads the dead down to Hades. Homer sings it in Odyssey 24.
At the river, Charon waits. The Greeks buried their dead with a coin to pay him: the obol.
A dog carries the dead across the river of the underworld. The descent through nine levels takes four years.
Odin's Valkyries choose who falls in battle, and carry the chosen to Valhalla.
Yama found the path of the dead first. Now he rules them, and judges them.
Malak al-Mawt, named Azrael in tradition, draws the soul from the body at the appointed hour.
Which of them would you want waiting for you? Answer below.

caption:
Every culture that buried its dead sent someone to collect them.

In Egypt, Anubis weighed the heart against the feather of Ma'at.
In Greece, Hermes led the shades down, and Charon took the obol at the river.
The Aztecs buried a dog with the dead, to carry them across.
Odin's Valkyries chose the fallen. Yama judged. Azrael waited for the hour.

The Greeks called them psychopomps: guides of souls.

Which one would you want at your door? Answer below.
